reason: While the text does depict the conflict as national (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל against מִצְרַיִם), it is fundamentally and explicitly depicted as religious. God directly intervenes throughout the narrative, commands Moses, hardens Pharaoh's heart, parts the sea, and the stated purpose is explicitly theological: 'וְיָדְעוּ מִצְרַיִם כִּי אֲנִי יְהוָה' (Egypt will know that I am the Lord). The divine agency and religious purpose are central to the narrative, not absent. The statement incorrectly negates the religious dimension entirely.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
